proofs.proof_tex:
Let
\[
s_n=\frac{n\log(d_n+1)}{d_n^2}=\frac1{r(n,d_n)}.
\]
The degree-growth and degree-lower assumptions imply \(s_n\to\infty\).  By Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}balanced\mbox{-}packing}\), there is a universal \(C_\beta<\infty\) such that the events
\[
E_n=\{\beta(G_n)\le C_\beta s_n\}
\]
satisfy \(\Pr(E_n)\to1\).  On \(E_n\), Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\mbox{-}bayes\mbox{-}converse}\) gives
\[
R(G_n)\ge\frac1{12\{\beta(G_n)+2\}}
\ge\frac1{12(C_\beta+1)s_n}
=\frac1{12(C_\beta+1)}\,
\frac{d_n^2}{n\log(d_n+1)}
\tag{17}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), where the second inequality uses \(s_n\ge2\).  Because Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}balanced\mbox{-}bayes\mbox{-}converse}\) lower-bounds the infimum in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\), (17) applies simultaneously to every graph-dependent design and measurable estimator.

For the upper side, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}retuned\mbox{-}seed\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}rate}\) and the degree-growth assumption show that, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every simple \(d_n\)-regular realization \(G\), the selected one-shot procedure is defined on the branch \(M_n<n\) and satisfies
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}
\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n}.
\tag{18}
\]
Its assignment law and estimator are graph-measurable finite maps by the same lemma.  They are therefore feasible competitors in the infimum defining \(R(G)\), and (18) implies \(R(G)\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}d_n^2/n\) for every such \(G\).  Taking
\(c=\{12(C_\beta+1)\}^{-1}\) and \(C=C_{\mathrm{rob}}\), the two inequalities hold simultaneously on \(E_n\).  Since \(\Pr(E_n)\to1\), the asserted probability limit follows.  The two displayed scales differ by exactly \(\log(d_n+1)\), so the proof supplies a bracket rather than a matched frontier.

First, the endpoint second-moment restrictions and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
|\mu_1|^2\le\frac1n\sum_i a_i^2\le1,
\qquad
|\mu_0|^2\le\frac1n\sum_i b_i^2\le1.
\]
Consequently \(|\tau_n|=|\mu_1-\mu_0|\le2\), so intersecting an interval with \([-2,2]\) cannot remove the true estimand.

We next verify the finite risk certificate, including its boundary branch.  If \(M_n\ge n\), Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}certified\mbox{-}procedure}\) returns \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=\mu_1\).  Its error is \(\mu_0\), whence
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
=\mu_0^2\le1=\overline U(G).
\tag{19}
\]
No inverse probability is formed on this branch.  If \(M_n<n\) and \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}retuned\mbox{-}seed\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}rate}\), applied with \(s=k_n\), gives
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
\le U(G,k_n)=\overline U(G).
\tag{20}
\]
If \(M_n<n\) but \(U(G,k_n)>1\), the procedure again uses the all-treated report, and (19) gives the same conclusion with \(\overline U(G)=1\).  Thus in every finite case
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
\le\overline U(G).
\tag{21}
\]
Every formed seed count is at least one, so \(U(G,k_n)\ge2/k_n>0\); on either fallback branch \(\overline U(G)=1\).  Hence \(\overline U(G)>0\) in every case.
For every \(t>0\), nonnegativity gives
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
\ge t^2\Pr_{\mathcal D_G}\!\left\{
|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n|>t\mid G
\right\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\sqrt{\overline U(G)/\alpha}\) and using (21) yields
\[
\Pr_{\mathcal D_G}\!\left\{
|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n|
>\sqrt{\overline U(G)/\alpha}\mid G
\right\}\le\alpha.
\]
Together with \(|\tau_n|\le2\) and Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\mbox{-}set}\), this is exactly the asserted finite conditional coverage.

Under the degree-growth assumption, Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}retuned\mbox{-}seed\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}rate}\) gives, uniformly over every simple regular realization and for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\overline U(G)\le U(G,k_n)
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}d_n^2/n.
\]
Taking square roots gives the displayed robust half-width.  It tends to zero for fixed \(\alpha\) because \(d_n/\sqrt n\to0\).

Finally assume the Boolean conjecture stated in the theorem.  On its norm event, the conditional part of Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}retuned\mbox{-}seed\mbox{-}certificate\mbox{-}rate}\) and the graph-based minimization over the two candidate counts give
\(U(G_n,k_n)\le C_Lr(n,d_n)\).  The finite coverage argument already applies to this same selected procedure.  On the norm event its untruncated half-width is at most
\[
\sqrt{C_Lr(n,d_n)/\alpha}
=\sqrt{C_L}\,
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n\log(d_n+1)}}.
\]
The conjecture says that the norm event has probability tending to one over \(G_n\), proving precisely the conditional final clause and no unconditional logarithmic refinement.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every finite simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\), let \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\) for \(i\ne j\).  Then
\[
B_2(G)_{ii}=1,
\qquad
B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})
\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}{r}
\quad(i\ne j).
\]
Thus the centered Boolean collision expansion contains common-neighbor shapes of every order \(1\le r\le d_n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix distinct \(i,j\).  By the definition of matrix multiplication, \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\) is the number of common neighbors of \(i\) and \(j\); in particular, \(c_{ij}\) is an integer in \(\{0,\ldots,d_n\}\).  If \(A_{G,ij}=1\), then \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)=1\), and both sides of the asserted off-diagonal identity equal one.  If \(A_{G,ij}=0\), then \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\) holds exactly when \(c_{ij}\ge1\).  The binomial theorem gives, for every integer \(c\in\{0,\ldots,d_n\}\),
\[
\mathbf 1\{c\ge1\}=1-(1-1)^c
=\sum_{r=1}^{c}(-1)^{r+1}\binom cr
=\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom cr,
\]
where \(\binom cr=0\) for \(r>c\).  Substitution of \(c=c_{ij}\) proves the off-diagonal formula.  Finally, \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,i)=0\), so Definition~\(B_2(G)_{ii}=\mathbf 1\{\operatorname{dist}_G(i,i)\le2\}\) gives \(B_2(G)_{ii}=1\).  The summation index ranges up to \(d_n\), proving the last assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: This exact identity exposes the unbounded common-neighbor orders that the unresolved Boolean operator conjecture must control.
added_lemmas.gap: Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices treats fixed graph-matrix shapes; the identity shows why a uniform resummation is additionally required here.
added_lemmas.consumer: The identity makes the remaining spectral limitation auditable without treating it as an established rate bound.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every finite simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\) with \(M_n<n\), and for every integer \(s\ge1\), form the \(s\)-seed analogues of the seed design and observed-data Rao--Blackwell estimator by replacing \(k_n\) by \(s\).  Define
\[
\mathcal U_G(s)=\frac{2}{s}+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-s}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)}.
\]
The analogue is unbiased for \(\tau_n\), and
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}
\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau_s-\tau_n)^2\mid G\right]
\le \mathcal U_G(s).
\]
Consequently, there is a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm{rob}}\), depending only on the fixed \(c_0\), such that every sequence satisfying \(d_n\ge3\) and \(d_n/\sqrt n\to0\) obeys, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every simple \(d_n\)-regular \(G\),
\[
M_n<n,
\qquad
U(G,k_n)\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n},
\qquad
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}
\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G\right]
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n}.
\]
Moreover, for every fixed \(L<\infty\), if
\(\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\), then the log-tuned choice
\[
k_n^\sharp=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(d_n+1)}{4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}}
\right\rfloor\right\}
\]
satisfies \(\mathcal U_G(k_n^\sharp)\le C_L r(n,d_n)\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), where \(C_L<\infty\) depends only on \(L\).  Because the actual count \(k_n\) minimizes the certificate over \(\{\widetilde k_n,k_n^\sharp\}\), the same event implies \(U(G,k_n)\le C_Lr(n,d_n)\).  The assignment probabilities, Rao--Blackwell weights, and both candidate certificates are finite computations obtained by enumerating the ordered seed tuples.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(S_i=\{v\in V_n:\operatorname{dist}_G(i,v)\le2\}\), \(m_i=|S_i|\), and \(q_i=1-m_i/n\).  A radius-two ball in a simple \(d_n\)-regular graph contains at most
\[
1+d_n+d_n(d_n-1)=d_n^2+1=M_n
\tag{1}
\]
vertices.  Thus \(M_n<n\) implies \(q_i\ge1-M_n/n>0\) for every \(i\), which justifies every inverse probability below.

Fix an integer \(s\ge1\), and let \(J_1,\ldots,J_s\) be independent uniform vertices.  If \(J_\ell=i\), then all vertices in \(N_G[i]\) are treated, so arbitrary neighborhood interference gives \(y_i(Z)=a_i\).  Hence the raw seed average
\[
\widetilde\mu_{1,s}=\frac1s\sum_{\ell=1}^s a_{J_\ell}
\]
is observable after retaining the seeds and satisfies
\[
\mathbb E(\widetilde\mu_{1,s}\mid G)=\mu_1,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\widetilde\mu_{1,s}\mid G)
=\frac1s\left\{\frac1n\sum_i a_i^2-\mu_1^2\right\}\le\frac1s
\tag{2}
\]
by the treated endpoint second-moment bound.  Conditional on the union assignment, the Rao--Blackwell weights in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}rb\mbox{-}estimator}\) give
\[
\widehat\mu_{1,s}
=\mathbb E(\widetilde\mu_{1,s}\mid Z,G)
=\sum_i w_{i,s}(Z;G)y_i(Z).
\]
Indeed, whenever the conditional multiplicity of \(i\) is positive, \(i\) is fully treated-exposed under that union assignment, so the displayed observed outcome equals \(a_i\).  The tower property and the law of total variance applied to (2) therefore yield
\[
\mathbb E(\widehat\mu_{1,s}\mid G)=\mu_1,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\mu_{1,s}\mid G)\le s^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]

Unit \(i\) is fully control-exposed exactly when every seed avoids \(S_i\).  Therefore its exposure probability is \(q_i^s>0\), and arbitrary neighborhood interference makes the control Horvitz--Thompson mean
\[
\widehat\mu_{0,s}=\frac1n\sum_i
\frac{\mathbf 1\{i\in C_G(Z)\}b_i}{q_i^s}
\]
observable and unbiased for \(\mu_0\).  Write \(H=B_2(G)B_2(G)^{\mathsf T}\), so \(H_{ij}=|S_i\cap S_j|\).  One seed avoids \(S_i\cup S_j\) with probability
\[
q_{ij}=1-\frac{m_i+m_j-H_{ij}}n.
\]
Since \(q_iq_j=(1-m_i/n)(1-m_j/n)\), direct subtraction gives
\[
\frac{q_{ij}}{q_iq_j}-1
=\frac{n^{-1}H_{ij}-n^{-2}m_im_j}{q_iq_j}
=K_{G,ij},
\tag{4}
\]
where the last equality follows from \(B_2(G)\iota_n=(m_i)_i\) and the definition of \(P_n\).  Independence of the \(s\) seeds now gives the normalized control-exposure covariance matrix
\[
Q^{(s)}_{G,ij}
=\frac{q_{ij}^s}{q_i^sq_j^s}-1
=(1+K_{G,ij})^s-1
=\sum_{r=1}^s\binom sr K_{G,ij}^r.
\tag{5}
\]

The matrix \(K_G\) is positive semidefinite because it is the Gram matrix
\[
K_G=\frac1n
\{D_q(G)^{-1}B_2(G)P_n\}
\{D_q(G)^{-1}B_2(G)P_n\}^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{6}
\]
If \(K_{G,ij}=\langle u_i,u_j\rangle\), then
\(K_{G,ij}^r=\langle u_i^{\otimes r},u_j^{\otimes r}\rangle\); hence every Schur power in (5), and therefore \(Q_G^{(s)}\), is positive semidefinite.  Moreover,
\[
K_{G,ii}=\frac{(m_i/n)(1-m_i/n)}{q_i^2}
=\frac{m_i/n}{1-m_i/n}
\le\delta:=\frac{M_n}{n(1-M_n/n)}.
\tag{7}
\]
For completeness, if \(D\succeq0\), writing \(D_{ij}=\sum_t v_{ti}v_{tj}\) shows
\(D\circ H=\sum_t\operatorname{diag}(v_t)H\operatorname{diag}(v_t)\).  Thus for symmetric \(H\),
\[
\|D\circ H\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\max_iD_{ii}\,\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{8}
\]
Apply (8) with \(D=K_G^{\circ(r-1)}\) and \(H=K_G\), using (7), to obtain
\(\|K_G^{\circ r}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta^{r-1}\|K_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Also (6), \(q_i\ge1-M_n/n\), and \(\|P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) imply
\[
\|K_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}
{n(1-M_n/n)^2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Summing (5), then using (7)--(9) and \(1+\delta=(1-M_n/n)^{-1}\), gives
\[
\lambda_{\max}(Q_G^{(s)})
\le
\frac{\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}
{M_n(1-M_n/n)}
\{(1-M_n/n)^{-s}-1\}.
\tag{10}
\]
The control endpoint bound gives \(\|b\|_2^2\le n\), so
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat\mu_{0,s}\mid G)
=n^{-2}b^{\mathsf T}Q_G^{(s)}b
\le
\frac{\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
\{(1-M_n/n)^{-s}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)}.
\tag{11}
\]
Both endpoint estimators are unbiased.  Combining (3) and (11) with
\(\operatorname{Var}(X-Y)\le2\operatorname{Var}(X)+2\operatorname{Var}(Y)\) proves the finite bound by \(\mathcal U_G(s)\).

We next specialize.  Put \(x=M_n/n\) and \(h=-\log(1-x)\).  The degree-growth assumption and \(d_n\ge3\) imply
\[
x=\frac{d_n^2+1}{n}\le\frac{10}{9}\frac{d_n^2}{n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{12}
\]
Consequently, eventually \(x\le1/2\), \(h\le2x\), and \(c_0/h\ge2\).  On this eventual range the maximum in the definition of \(\widetilde k_n\) is inactive and
\[
\widetilde k_n=\left\lfloor\frac{c_0}{h}\right\rfloor
\ge\frac{c_0}{2h},
\qquad
\widetilde k_nh\le c_0.
\tag{13}
\]
The matrix \(B_2(G)\) is symmetric and nonnegative, and (1) bounds all its row and column sums by \(M_n\).  Hence
\[
\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\|B_2(G)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\sqrt{\|B_2(G)\|_1\|B_2(G)\|_\infty}
\le M_n.
\tag{14}
\]
Equations (13)--(14) yield
\[
\frac{2}{\widetilde k_n}\le\frac{8M_n}{c_0n},
\qquad
(1-x)^{-\widetilde k_n}-1=e^{\widetilde k_nh}-1\le e^{c_0}-1,
\]
and therefore
\[
\mathcal U_G(\widetilde k_n)
\le\left\{\frac8{c_0}+4(e^{c_0}-1)\right\}\frac{M_n}{n}
\le C_{\mathrm{rob}}\frac{d_n^2}{n},
\tag{15}
\]
where one may take
\(C_{\mathrm{rob}}=\frac{10}{9}\{8/c_0+4(e^{c_0}-1)\}\).  The selection rule gives
\[
U(G,k_n)=\mathcal U_G(k_n)\le\mathcal U_G(\widetilde k_n).
\]
The right side of (15) tends to zero, so eventually \(U(G,k_n)\le1\).  The certified procedure then selects the seed estimator, and its asserted risk bound follows from the finite part of the proof.

Finally suppose \(\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\), and put
\(s=k_n^\sharp\).  By (12), eventually the quantity inside the floor is at least two.  Hence
\[
\frac2s\le\frac{32x}{\log(d_n+1)},
\qquad
sh\le\frac14\log(d_n+1),
\]
so that
\[
\mathcal U_G(s)
\le\frac{32M_n}{n\log(d_n+1)}
+\frac{4L^2d_n^{7/2}(d_n+1)^{1/4}}{nM_n}.
\tag{16}
\]
Here we used \(x\le1/2\).  Since \(M_n\ge d_n^2\), \(M_n\le(10/9)d_n^2\), and, for \(d_n\ge3\), both \((d_n+1)^{1/4}\le(4/3)^{1/4}d_n^{1/4}\) and \(\log(d_n+1)\le2d_n^{1/4}\), the right side of (16) is at most \(C_Ld_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\).  This proves the conditional log-tuned bound.
The selection rule also gives
\[
U(G,k_n)\le\mathcal U_G(k_n^\sharp)\le C_Lr(n,d_n)
\]
on the stated norm event.

For either candidate count, there are finitely many ordered seed tuples, namely \(n^s\).  Enumerating them computes their union assignments, assignment masses, conditional multiplicities, all exposure probabilities, and all Rao--Blackwell weights.  The squared operator norm is the largest eigenvalue of the rational symmetric matrix \(B_2(G)P_nB_2(G)^{\mathsf T}\), hence is a real algebraic number.  Exact root isolation and algebraic sign comparison decide which of the two displayed certificate scores is smaller, with the stipulated deterministic tie break; rational interval enclosures certify the resulting numerical value to any requested accuracy.  Thus every claimed object is a finite graph computation.

The smallest admissible regular instance is \((n,d_n)=(4,3)\).  There \(M_n=10\ge n\), so the compiler forms no seed ratio and uses the point-mass all-treated design.  Its error is \(\mu_0\), and the endpoint bound gives \(\mu_0^2\le1\), with equality for \(b_i=1\) for all \(i\); thus the fallback certificate is exact on this enumerable instance even though the fallback estimator need not be unbiased for \(\tau_n\).  At the opposite boundary, every step in (12)--(15) uses only \(d_n^2/n\to0\).  No conclusion is asserted when \(d_n\) is proportional to \(\sqrt n\), where \(x\) need not vanish.
added_lemmas.justification: The lemma derives the unconditional robust upper rate from the primitive row-sum geometry and isolates the sharper logarithmic certificate as a genuinely conditional refinement.
added_lemmas.gap: No random-regular spectral theorem is needed for the robust bound; the only unproved improvement is the Boolean radius-two norm conjecture.
added_lemmas.consumer: The finite compiler can choose between the robust and log-tuned counts before assignment and certify a one-round full-GATE error bound on the revealed network.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original matched upper rate requires the unresolved Boolean operator conjecture.  The balanced-packing converse proves the displayed lower scale, while the robust seed-count candidate and the deterministic row-sum norm bound prove the same-assumption upper scale of order \(d_n^2/n\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every finite revealed graph \(G\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), and every \(y\in\mathcal M_n(G)\), the retuned selected procedure satisfies
\[
\Pr_{\mathcal D_G}\!\left\{
\tau_n\in\mathcal C_\alpha(G,Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\mid G
\right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For every admissible degree sequence and every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the untruncated certificate half-width is, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and uniformly over every simple \(d_n\)-regular realization,
\[
\sqrt{\overline U(G)/\alpha}
\le \sqrt{C_{\mathrm{rob}}}\,
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n}}=o(1).
\]
If the unresolved Boolean conjecture holds, namely if some universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies
\[
\Pr\!\left\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
then the same graph-selected procedure has, with probability tending to one over \(G_n\), half-width at most
\[
\sqrt{C_L}\,
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n\log(d_n+1)}}.
\]
The sharper logarithmic radius is conditional only; the procedure's unconditional guarantee remains the robust radius above.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Finite conditional coverage remains exact, but the unconditional certificate radius supplied without the Boolean conjecture is \(O(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n})\).  The same graph-selected procedure has the logarithmically sharper radius only under the explicit conjectural norm event.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Fix once and for all \(c_0\in(0,1)\).  On the branch \(M_n<n\), set
\[
\widetilde k_n=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lfloor\frac{c_0}{-\log(1-M_n/n)}\right\rfloor\right\},
\qquad
k_n^\sharp=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(d_n+1)}{4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}}
\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
For \(s\in\{\widetilde k_n,k_n^\sharp\}\), compute the graph-only score
\[
\Gamma_G(s)=\frac2s+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-s}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)},
\]
and let \(k_n\) be the smaller minimizer of \(\Gamma_G(s)\) over these two candidates.  Draw \(J_1,\ldots,J_{k_n}\) independently and uniformly from \(V_n\), and assign
\[
Z^{\mathrm{seed}}_v=\mathbf 1\!\left\{v\in\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{k_n}N_G[J_\ell]\right\}.
\]
On the branch \(M_n\ge n\), this seed design is not formed.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The design adds a fixed-exponent robust candidate and selects the better graph certificate between it and the log-tuned candidate, yielding the unconditional upper rate without discarding a possible sharper certificate.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
On the branch \(M_n<n\), use the graph-selected count \(k_n\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}seed\mbox{-}design}\) and form
\[
K_G=n^{-1}D_q(G)^{-1}B_2(G)P_nB_2(G)^{\mathsf T}D_q(G)^{-1},
\qquad
Q_G=\sum_{r=1}^{k_n}\binom{k_n}{r}K_G^{\circ r},
\]
and
\[
U(G,k_n)=\frac{2}{k_n}+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-k_n}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)}.
\]
These objects are not formed on the branch \(M_n\ge n\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The certificate is synchronized with the graph-selected seed count and is formed only on its positive-exposure branch.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For distinct \(i,j\in V_n\), put \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\).  The handle \(\mathsf H_B\) records the exact Booleanization
\[
B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})
\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}{r},
\qquad B_2(G)_{ii}=1,
\]
followed by centering with \(P_n\).  It is a diagnostic decomposition, not an operator-norm bound: its terms contain \(K_{2,r}\)-type common-neighbor shapes with unbounded \(r\), whose uniform resummation over \(3\le d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) remains unresolved.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former handle suggested a switching resummation without establishing it.  The corrected construction records the exact Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion and labels the uniform resummation as unresolved.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: First compare \(M_n\) with \(n\).  If \(M_n\ge n\), form none of \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\); assign \(Z=\mathbf 1_n\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}y_i(\mathbf 1_n)\), and set \(\overline U(G)=1\).  If \(M_n<n\), compute the two candidates and graph-only scores from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}seed\mbox{-}design}\), and use their smaller certificate minimizer \(k_n\).  Compute \(U(G,k_n)\).  When \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), use \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and set \(\overline U(G)=U(G,k_n)\); otherwise return the same all-treated fallback and set \(\overline U(G)=1\).

proposed.name: Retuned with-replacement neighborhood-seed design
proposed.construction:
Fix once and for all \(c_0\in(0,1)\).  On the branch \(M_n<n\), set
\[
\widetilde k_n=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lfloor\frac{c_0}{-\log(1-M_n/n)}\right\rfloor\right\},
\qquad
k_n^\sharp=\max\!\left\{1,\left\lfloor
\frac{\log(d_n+1)}{4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}}
\right\rfloor\right\}.
\]
For \(s\in\{\widetilde k_n,k_n^\sharp\}\), compute the graph-only score
\[
\Gamma_G(s)=\frac2s+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-s}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)},
\]
and let \(k_n\) be the smaller minimizer of \(\Gamma_G(s)\) over these two candidates.  Draw \(J_1,\ldots,J_{k_n}\) independently and uniformly from \(V_n\), and assign
\[
Z^{\mathrm{seed}}_v=\mathbf 1\!\left\{v\in\bigcup_{\ell=1}^{k_n}N_G[J_\ell]\right\}.
\]
On the branch \(M_n\ge n\), this seed design is not formed.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete definition now carries both candidate counts, the graph-only selection rule, and its branch boundary.

proposed.name: Selected-count exact Schur covariance and deterministic risk certificate
proposed.construction:
On the branch \(M_n<n\), use the graph-selected count \(k_n\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}seed\mbox{-}design}\) and form
\[
K_G=n^{-1}D_q(G)^{-1}B_2(G)P_nB_2(G)^{\mathsf T}D_q(G)^{-1},
\qquad
Q_G=\sum_{r=1}^{k_n}\binom{k_n}{r}K_G^{\circ r},
\]
and
\[
U(G,k_n)=\frac{2}{k_n}+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-k_n}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)}.
\]
These objects are not formed on the branch \(M_n\ge n\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete certificate definition now explicitly uses the graph-selected count and positive-exposure branch.

proposed.name: Centered Boolean collision diagnostic
proposed.construction:
For distinct \(i,j\in V_n\), put \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\).  The handle \(\mathsf H_B\) records the exact Booleanization
\[
B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})
\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}{r},
\qquad B_2(G)_{ii}=1,
\]
followed by centering with \(P_n\).  It is a diagnostic decomposition, not an operator-norm bound: its terms contain \(K_{2,r}\)-type common-neighbor shapes with unbounded \(r\), whose uniform resummation over \(3\le d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) remains unresolved.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete post-image exposes the exact expansion while making clear that no operator estimate is embedded in the definition.

proposed.name: Graph-selected certified one-shot procedure
proposed.construction: First compare \(M_n\) with \(n\).  If \(M_n\ge n\), form none of \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\); assign \(Z=\mathbf 1_n\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=n^{-1}\sum_{i\in V_n}y_i(\mathbf 1_n)\), and set \(\overline U(G)=1\).  If \(M_n<n\), compute the two candidates and graph-only scores from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}seed\mbox{-}design}\), and use their smaller certificate minimizer \(k_n\).  Compute \(U(G,k_n)\).  When \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), use \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), report \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{cert}}=\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and set \(\overline U(G)=U(G,k_n)\); otherwise return the same all-treated fallback and set \(\overline U(G)=1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The full procedure is synchronized with the two-candidate graph selection while retaining the branch-safe all-treated fallback.

proposed.justification: This gives a full two-arm, all-procedure lower bound and an explicit one-shot upper design, reducing the known polynomial gap to a logarithmic gap.
proposed.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax has the same \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale but only a \(d_n/n\) lower scale; the remaining logarithmic gap is not closed here.
proposed.consumer: ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice motivates using the bracket to assess the robust precision range for a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular experiment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency on the unresolved Boolean question is removed; the replacement depends only on the proved packing converse and selected seed certificate.

proposed.statement:
For every finite revealed graph \(G\), every \(0<\alpha<1\), and every \(y\in\mathcal M_n(G)\), the retuned selected procedure satisfies
\[
\Pr_{\mathcal D_G}\!\left\{
\tau_n\in\mathcal C_\alpha(G,Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\mid G
\right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For every admissible degree sequence and every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the untruncated certificate half-width is, for all sufficiently large \(n\) and uniformly over every simple \(d_n\)-regular realization,
\[
\sqrt{\overline U(G)/\alpha}
\le \sqrt{C_{\mathrm{rob}}}\,
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n}}=o(1).
\]
If the unresolved Boolean conjecture holds, namely if some universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies
\[
\Pr\!\left\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
then the same graph-selected procedure has, with probability tending to one over \(G_n\), half-width at most
\[
\sqrt{C_L}\,
\frac{d_n}{\sqrt{\alpha n\log(d_n+1)}}.
\]
The sharper logarithmic radius is conditional only; the procedure's unconditional guarantee remains the robust radius above.
proposed.justification: The graph-computable risk certificate yields finite-sample design-based coverage under endpoint second moments alone and a robust shrinking radius without a Gaussian approximation.
proposed.gap: The unconditional radius is of order \(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n}\); the logarithmically sharper radius remains conditional on the unresolved Boolean norm conjecture.
proposed.consumer: The next one-round random-regular public-goods experiment receives a precomputable honest error bar for the full all-free versus all-fixed contrast.

proposed.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim\mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for random \(d\)-regular \(G\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the sum of endpoint empirical second moments.
Algorithm 4 is the paper's polynomial approximation design, Proposition 4.3 states its guarantee, and Theorem C.11 is the imported 2-approximation for Partial Vertex Cover used as a subroutine.
Theorem 4.8 bounds GATE Horvitz--Thompson variance for randomized one-hop-max clustering under bounded outcomes and restricted growth.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance bounds and gives convex programs selecting minimally conservative bounds for linear estimators.

prose_updates.tldr: For a revealed uniform simple \(d_n\)-regular network under unrestricted arbitrary neighborhood interference and endpoint empirical second-moment bounds, the proved result is the high-probability bracket \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\).  The lower side is design-uniform.  For the upper side, a one-shot neighborhood-seed design selects the better graph certificate from a fixed-exponent robust count and a log-tuned count; the robust candidate needs only the deterministic row-sum bound.  The selected procedure gives finite conditional coverage and unconditional radius \(O(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n})=o(1)\) for fixed \(\alpha\).  Its sharper logarithmic radius is conditional on an unresolved Boolean radius-two operator conjecture; no matched minimax order or strict upper-scale improvement is claimed.

project_justification.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, leaves \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) for the same random-regular full-GATE problem.  The present result raises the all-procedure lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), reducing the polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap to a logarithmic gap while retaining the published upper order.
project_justification.niche: Balanced simultaneous endpoint exposure supplies a two-arm Bayes converse, while certificate-based selection between fixed-exponent and log-tuned neighborhood-seed counts makes the exact Schur construction robust without discarding a possible sharper rate.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the balanced-packing lower scale, constructs an observed-data Rao--Blackwell seed estimator, and includes a fixed-exponent candidate for which the elementary bound \(\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le d_n^2+1\) yields the uniform \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale.  The graph chooses the smaller of this certificate and the log-tuned certificate before assignment.  A branch-safe compiler and a Markov risk interval provide finite-sample inference; the remaining logarithmic improvement is isolated as a conjecture rather than assumed.

sampling_model.design: The graph \(G=G_n\) is revealed first.  On \(M_n<n\), the experimenter fixes \(c_0\in(0,1)\), computes the robust candidate \(\widetilde k_n=\max\{1,\lfloor c_0/[-\log(1-M_n/n)]\rfloor\}\) and the log-tuned candidate \(k_n^\sharp=\max\{1,\lfloor\log(d_n+1)/[4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}]\rfloor\}\), and chooses the candidate with smaller graph certificate before drawing seeds.  It then treats the union of the selected number of uniform seeds' closed neighborhoods.  The finite fallback assigns every unit treatment when the positive-exposure branch is unavailable or the selected certificate exceeds one.

The present balanced-exposure converse improves its lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) but retains its upper order, leaving a logarithmic gap.  Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 motivate finite design computation but do not give the graph-selected seed certificate.  KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies a generic conflict-graph variance scale; the current unconditional upper bound does not strictly improve that scale.  UganderYin2023RGCR studies randomized graph cluster designs under bounded outcomes and a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure, rather than unrestricted minimax risk.  AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping foundation.  BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich supports the proved random-regular packing transfer in its verified degree regime.  Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, treats graph-matrix shapes but does not uniformly resum the unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type terms in the Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion.  BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control adjacency spectra, not this Boolean correction.  HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance optimizes conservative bounds for fixed linear estimators and does not choose the minimax design.  ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice remains the prospective application: a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment can use the robust certificate without assuming its behavioral outcomes attain worst-case risk.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For \(i\ne j\), let \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\).  The exact identity is \(B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}r\), with \(B_2(G)_{ii}=1\).  The unresolved conjecture is that some universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies \(\Pr\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\}\to1\) uniformly over every admissible degree sequence.  Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, does not by itself uniformly resum these unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type shapes.  Accordingly the conjecture is not a premise of the unconditional risk or confidence theorem; it yields only the separately labeled logarithmic refinement.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established same-assumption result is a logarithmic minimax bracket, not a matched frontier.  The robust candidate in the graph-selected seed design gives an unconditional \(d_n^2/n\) upper bound on every sufficiently large simple \(d_n\)-regular graph, while the random-regular balanced-packing result gives the high-probability \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) lower bound over all procedures.  The Boolean operator estimate remains an explicit conjecture; if true, the selected design automatically uses a certificate no larger than the log-tuned one.  Seed probabilities and inverse weights are formed only on \(M_n<n\); the complementary branch uses an all-treated fallback.  The result concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE.  It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or a claim that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case.
